_why_this_file_exists: Gate 4N-I16's containment test iterated gen.INLINE_POLICY_ROLE_ARNS as its definition of
'the declared roles' — the policy's own Resource list. Allow, deny-fence and test
expectation therefore moved together, and appending an arbitrary attacker ARN to that list
left the whole suite and nine guard scripts green. A ceiling derived from the grant it is
_authority: Authored from the architecture requirement that a role is writable ONLY IF the composition
intends it to carry an inline policy. NOT parsed from the .tf files and NOT read from any
generated policy — those are the OBSERVED side. Changing this file is a reviewable diff.
The .tf parser in scripts/terraform_role_inventory.py is a THIRD, separate cross-check:
declared (parsed) vs expected (this file) vs generated (policy) must all agree.

_i24c_identity_requirement: GATE 4N-I24C, finding I24C-04. Suffix rules pin how identities are SPELLED, not WHICH
identities may be written. Two executed exploits followed: a role named
'<prefix>-evil-api-task' satisfied endswith('api-task') and entered BOTH sides as
CORRECTLY_WRITABLE clean; and a role the .tf parser MISSED vanished from both sides with
zero problems (FAIL-OPEN), because unknown_roles iterated the parsed set. These EXACT names
are the requirement. A name not listed here is UNKNOWN and UNKNOWN is a finding.
